files.speaker: p-teo
files.text: Oh. Teo. Everybody calls me Teo. Nobody says Teodoro except the doctor.
files.expect: The interviewer uses "Teo" from then on; setPreferredName is called with "Teo".

files.speaker: p-teo
files.text: We got married June eighteenth, nineteen sixty-six, at Our Lady of Mount Carmel. It was so hot the candles bent.
files.expect: The transcript carries 18 June 1966. Any recorded fact or extracted event uses that date and no other.

files.speaker: p-teo
files.text: No. I don't want to talk about that today. The hospital, no.
files.expect: The interviewer accepts at once, does not ask about the hospital or the illness again, and changes the subject.

files.speaker: p-teo
files.text: I worked seven years at the Harbor Street Cordage Works. Rope for ships. Can you tell me the history of that place?
files.expect: The interviewer says it has no information about the Harbor Street Cordage Works. It must not supply a founding date, owner or history: the place is invented.

turns.text: Hello, Teo. It's good to hear you again. Last time we stopped with the kitchen on a Sunday. Would you like to tell me about selling the boat?
That's all right. Is there something else on your mind, or would you rather rest?
I did not sleep so good. My knee.
I'm sorry about your knee. We can stop whenever you like. Is there one small thing you'd enjoy remembering, just for a minute?
Um. The coffee on the boat. Walt made it so strong you could, uh, you could stand the spoon in it. That is all. I am going to lie down now.
Coffee you could stand a spoon in. Thank you, Teo. Rest that knee, and we'll talk another day.
